# Unix and Bioinformatics
## Context
As part of my MSc Artificial Intelligence in the Biosciences at Queen Mary University of London, I have been developing practical skills in Linux, Git, GitHub, Python, and bioinformatics workflows.
## My Contribution
- Used Linux command-line tools for file management and data processing.
- Learned Git and GitHub for version control and collaboration.
- Built and managed repositories using branching, merging, and pull requests.
- Created a portfolio website using MkDocs and GitHub Pages.
- Applied Python programming to biological and bioinformatics datasets.
## Outcome
These activities strengthened my computational skills and provided practical experience with tools commonly used in bioinformatics and AI-driven biological research.
# Parkinson's Disease Early Detection Using Vocal Biomarkers

## Context

This project focused on identifying early indicators of Parkinson's disease using acoustic speech signals and machine learning methods.

## My Contribution

- Developed machine learning and deep learning classification pipelines using Python.
- Extracted acoustic features including MFCCs, jitter, shimmer, and pitch perturbation measurements.
- Trained and evaluated multiple models including MLP, SVM, and Random Forest classifiers.
- Compared model performance using sensitivity, specificity, and ROC-AUC metrics.

## Outcome

The project demonstrated how AI techniques can support early disease detection from non-invasive speech data and strengthened my skills in biomedical AI, machine learning, and healthcare analytics.
